full_judgment:
2. The petitioner who comes of a lower middle class family has been carrying on the business of a small stationery shop at Comilla for the last 20 years. He is to maintain a large family including six school and college-going sons and daughters. He has little education and can only just read and write. He never indulged in any politics nor ever associated with any political party on 4-6-73 a contingent of police force visited the village home of the petitioner and carried out a thorough search but could not find any incriminating article. He was arrested on the same date under section 54 Cr P. C read with P.O 50 of 1972. Before he was put into the Dacca Central Jail, the petitioner was, after his arrest, kept in the police custody for 2 days at Comilla and seven days at Dacca. At Dacca he was taken to a private house in Gulshan residential area and was asked to make a statement in Bengali. On 13-6-73 he was brought to the Dacca Central Jail. On 3- 9-73 an order of detention was passed against him for 30 days and on expiry of the said period the detention was extended under sub-section (1) of section 17 of the said Public Safety Ordinance, 1958 for a period of 3 months commencing from 2-10-73. He was served with a copy of the grounds of detention which are as follows: 

 "Communication of rounds of detention u/s 19 of the Bangladesh Public Safety Ordinance 1958 (Ordinance No. LXXVIII of 1958) 

 In pursuance of section 19 of the Bangladesh Public Safety Ordinance (Ordinance No. LXXVIII of 1958), you, Md. Habibur Rahman alias Monu, s/o L. Moulana Wazuddin of Rampur, P S Chandpur, Dist. Comilla, arrested on 3-9-73 u/s 41 (1) of the Bangladesh Public Safety Ordinance, 1958 and at present detained in the Dacca Central Jail are hereby informed that your detention under sub-section (1) of section 17 of the said Ordinance, has been considered necessary on the following grounds: — 

 GOVERNMENT OF THE PEOPLE'S REPUBLIC OF BANGLADESH MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS, 

 WHEREAS the Government is satisfied that with a view to preventing Mr. Md Habibur Rahman alias Monu, s/o. Late Moulana Wazuddin of Rampur, P. S. Chandpur, Dist. Comilla from doing any act which is likely to prejudice the sovereignty and security of Bangladesh and to endanger public safety and the maintenance of public order it is necessary to make an order for his detention; 

 NOW, THEREFORE, in exercise of the power conferred by clause of subsection (1) of section 3 of the Special Powers Act, 1974 (Act No. XIV of 1974), the Government is pleased to direct that the said person be detained in the Dacca Central Jail for a period of 120 days from the date of his detention under this order. 

 8. So far as the order of detention passed on 14-2-74 is concerned it is seen that, unlike the other case referred to above (Criminal Misc. Case No. 190/73), the order recites "the Government is satisfied". This does not indicate the person who actually was satisfied and whose satisfaction is the satisfaction of the Government as required under section 17 (1) of the Ordinance since the Government is an abstract entity, it cannot have the satisfaction mentioned in section 17 (1) of the Ordinance. Somebody must actually have such satisfaction. Whoever he is, he must be authorized to exercise the statutory powers conferred by section 7 (1) of the Ordinance. We have not been shown any authority which empowered anybody to exercise such powers or the name of a person who has been so authorized. In the absence of such authority no per son could be said to have had the satisfaction as required under section 17 (1) of the Ordinance or consequently the power to pass an order of detention on having such satisfaction. In these circumstances we are unable to say that the order of detention passed, on 14-2-74 is bonfide or legal. Apart from these aspects relating to satisfaction the absence of materials other than the disclosure in the confession by the self-styled "General" Habib Khan definitely tends to show that the action of the detaining authority is malafide.
